correctness.rationale: The proof uses normalized radial moments m_n=1/(n+1)-q/(n+gamma+1); for q<1 the exact probability-mixture identity gives (1-q)(1-s)^2 K=1-q int u((1-s)/(1-us))^2 dmu with p=1+gamma/(1-q)>1. The maximum-modulus boundary computation gives u abs((1-s)/(1-us))^2 <=4u/(1+u)^2<1 for u in (0,1), proving strict disk and half-plane bounds; q=0 gives equality, q=1 has exact rational kernel and Cayley positivity. Both zeros and all parameter endpoints checked. The actual standalone path power_weight_verify.py passed 4,200 exact coefficient equalities and finite consistency tests; these are not treated as proof of the infinite claim. No unstated infinite certification or inaccessible source is needed to verify premises.

originality.rationale: Material comparison with arXiv:2609.24258v1, 1009.2806v1, 1703.05976v1 and 1802.01099v1 gives no theorem implying quantitative half-plane positivity for this complete strictly log-superharmonic power-deficit weight family. The earlier Hedenmalm criterion quoted and contrasted in Perala assumes logarithmic subharmonicity, whereas Delta log w is strictly negative for every q>0 at positive radii. Zeytuncu proves some decreasing radial weights have zeros but does not imply either answer for this fixed family. Available published records showed no dominating published result. Residual possibility of unindexed equivalent sources is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The radial Lu Qi-Keng question is mathematically nontrivial even for bounded, radially decreasing, equivalent weights: Zeytuncu constructs decreasing radial weights with zeros. This theorem gives a full continuous two-parameter zero-free family, including arbitrary positive real exponents and the boundary-degenerate endpoint, with an explicit uniform sharp half-plane estimate and a stronger disk certificate. The property is not an isolated numeric special case, cannot follow merely from weight comparability or radial monotonicity, and supplies a concrete benchmark for modern Bergman-weight parameter studies. The theorem does not require broad classification or downstream applications for its motivated structural value.
